original_source_text: As DRAM scales to higher density and I/O speeds, ensuring data correctness becomes increasingly difficult. Industry has responded with a three-layer stack: on-die ECC (O-ECC), link ECC (L-ECC), and system ECC (S-ECC). However, these layers have evolved independently, often duplicating redundancy, leaving coverage gaps, and occasionally interfering. We propose Cerberus, a cross-layer ECC co-design that unifies protection across device, link, and system while preserving the native role of each layer. At its core is an Encode-Once, Decode-Many (EODM) architecture: the controller performs a single encoding whose redundancy is reused by L-ECC for immediate write-path detection and retry, by O-ECC for in-device repair on reads, and by S-ECC for strong end-to-end recovery. Cerberus jointly designs complementary parity and syndrome structures, orders decoders, and allocates the correction budget to prevent miscorrection amplification and enable selective correction under tight redundancy constraints. Our evaluations show improved resilience to clustered and peripheral faults while reducing redundant overhead, underscoring the importance of coordinated cross-layer protection for next-generation memory systems, such as custom HBMs.

record_under_review.evidence_span: Cerberus co-designs on-die ECC, link ECC, and system ECC for dense, high-speed DRAM. Its Encode-Once, Decode-Many design reuses controller encoding for link-level write detection/retry, device repair on reads, and system-level end-to-end recovery. The paper combines complementary parity/syndrome structures, decoder ordering, and a correction budget intended to avoid miscorrection amplification and reports improved resilience to clustered and peripheral faults with reduced redundant overhead in an HBM context.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Dense high-speed DRAM and HBM-style memory stacks with on-die, link, and system ECC layers; results depend on the assumed fault model, interface organization, and controller/device cooperation.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact codeword layouts, fault-model probabilities, decoder latency, area/energy overhead, HBM generation, and quantitative baseline tables must be extracted from the full paper before making deployment or superiority claims.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: A cross-layer ECC architecture using Encode-Once, Decode-Many, complementary parity and syndrome structures, ordered decoding, and a correction budget that coordinates recovery across the memory stack.
record_under_review.problem: Independent evolution of on-die, link, and system ECC creates duplicated redundancy, gaps, and cross-layer interference as DRAM density and I/O speed increase.
record_under_review.title: Cerberus: Cross-Layer ECC Co-Design for Robust and Efficient Memory Protection
